summary: The prepared_gaia project implements a GAIA-inspired multi-agent system for cockroach detection using asyncio and a custom MessageBroker. Six agents (DetectionAgent/wk, PredictionAgent/pk, NotificationAgent/is, DisinfectionAgent/we, SimulationAgent/sim, GUIAgent/gui) are defined with role names matching the GAIA model. However, the MessageBroker communication infrastructure is entirely non-functional: agents write messages to broker queues but no agent ever reads from its own queue, making all inter-agent communication dead code. Additionally, requirement 5 (identifying high-activity zones) is not implemented, SensorDataMessage lacks a direct cockroach-count field, and all agents are hardcoded to a single room.

findings.description: The MessageBroker's receive_message() method is never called anywhere in the codebase. Every agent sends messages via broker.send_message() into queues that nobody reads. All defined inter-agent communication paths are dead code.
findings.evidence: main.py: MessageBroker.receive_message() defined at line 169 but never invoked; DetectionAgent.detector() calls broker.send_message() to 'is' and 'we' (lines 227-236) but NotificationAgent.my_behav() and DisinfectionAgent.my_behav() never call broker.receive_message()

findings.description: DetectionAgent and PredictionAgent each generate their own independent sensor readings internally instead of consuming data from SimulationAgent. SimulationAgent sends data to 'wk' and 'pk' queues, but those agents never read from them, so the SIM-to-WK/PK data flow is broken in both directions.
findings.evidence: main.py SimulationAgent.my_behav() lines 429-439: sends SENSOR_DATA_MSG to 'wk' and 'pk'; DetectionAgent.update_dorm_readings() lines 191-211: generates its own sensor data independently and sends to 'sim', not receiving from 'sim'

findings.description: NotificationAgent.my_behav() never checks for or reads detection/prediction messages from its queue. It unconditionally generates a hardcoded 'warning' notification for room_101 on every iteration, regardless of whether any detection occurred.
findings.evidence: main.py lines 336-357: NotificationAgent.my_behav() creates a hardcoded NotificationMessage('warning', 'Roach detection in room 101', ...) without reading from its broker queue

findings.description: DisinfectionAgent.my_behav() never reads disinfection requests sent by DetectionAgent. It unconditionally dispatches a hardcoded disinfection notification on every iteration.
findings.evidence: main.py lines 376-397: DisinfectionAgent.my_behav() creates a hardcoded DisinfectionMessage without reading from its broker queue; DetectionAgent.detector() sends DISINFECTION_MSG to 'we' (line 233) which is never consumed

findings.description: GUIAgent.event_collector() prints a static string but never reads from its registered broker queue, so no notifications sent to 'gui' are ever displayed or processed.
findings.evidence: main.py lines 477-483: `async def event_collector(self): await asyncio.sleep(1); print('GUI: Collecting events from agents')` — no broker.receive_message() call

findings.description: Requirement 5 — identifying locations with highest cockroach activity to optimise elimination — is not implemented. No agent maintains per-location activity statistics or produces a prioritised hotspot list.
findings.evidence: No location-aggregation logic exists in any agent; all activity is hardcoded to 'room_101' with no cross-room comparison

findings.description: SensorDataMessage does not include a cockroach-count field. The message models temperature, humidity, waste, and movement as proxy indicators, but the system never derives or transmits an explicit cockroach count, making requirement 3 (data must include number of detected individuals) only partially satisfied.
findings.evidence: main.py lines 19-35: SensorDataMessage fields are room_id, temperature, humidity, waste, movement — no cockroach_count

findings.description: Notifications only reach the GUI agent; there is no direct notification path to the pest-control company, building administration, or individual students as required. Notifications are routed only to 'gui'.
findings.evidence: main.py NotificationAgent.my_behav() line 348: `self.broker.send_message(self.name, 'gui', ...)` — no messages sent to administration or pest control agents

findings.description: The system only monitors a single hardcoded room ('room_101'). All six agents reference this constant; there is no mechanism to extend coverage to other rooms in the building.
findings.evidence: main.py DetectionAgent.__init__() line 186: `self.room_id = 'room_101'`; PredictionAgent.__init__() line 261: `self.room_id = 'room_101'`; SimulationAgent.__init__() line 415: `self.room_id = 'room_101'`

findings.description: KeyboardInterrupt is caught inside asyncio.gather() which does not propagate that exception reliably in all Python versions. The cancellation logic may not execute cleanly on SIGINT.
findings.evidence: main.py lines 518-524: `try: await asyncio.gather(*tasks) except KeyboardInterrupt: for task in tasks: task.cancel()`

findings.description: import time and import json are present but time is unused; json is used for json.dumps() only and messages are never deserialized with json.loads(), making the JSON encoding one-way and unverified.
findings.evidence: main.py line 5: `import time` (never used); all broker messages are serialised with json.dumps() but broker.receive_message() is never called, so json.loads() is never needed

findings.description: The AcknowledgeMessage mechanism is implemented but all acknowledgements are sent back to 'sim' which never reads from its queue. Acknowledge messages accumulate in an unconsumed queue indefinitely.
findings.evidence: main.py SimulationAgent registered at line 496 via broker.register_agent('sim'); DetectionAgent sends ACKNOWLEDGE_MSG to 'sim' (lines 209-211, 240-242) but SimulationAgent.my_behav() never calls receive_message()

missing_requirements: Identifying locations with the highest cockroach activity to optimise elimination actions (requirement 5) — no cross-location activity comparison or hotspot ranking is implemented.
logical_inconsistencies: MessageBroker queues are populated via send_message() but receive_message() is never called by any agent, making all defined communication paths non-functional.

SimulationAgent sends sensor data to WK and PK agents, but DetectionAgent and PredictionAgent generate their own independent sensor readings and also send data back to SIM, creating redundant and disconnected data flows.
NotificationAgent and DisinfectionAgent produce hardcoded output unconditionally rather than reacting to actual detection or disinfection-request messages.
All agents operate exclusively on 'room_101'; the multi-room monitoring premise of the requirements is architecturally impossible without structural changes.
implementation_risks: Because no agent reads from its broker queue, the MessageBroker queues will grow without bound as the system runs, eventually exhausting memory.
Hardcoded single-room logic means the system cannot be extended to cover additional rooms without significant refactoring of all six agents.
Notifications are only routed to the GUI layer; pest control, administration, and students are never notified directly, which would be a critical operational failure in production.
No tests exist; the entirely non-functional communication infrastructure could not be caught by any automated means.
